note: Families of terminal behaviour the Terminal Lab could exercise, and whether lab.rs's observe() records each one's effect: the text and style runs of every screen row and of up to 64 history rows, the cursor's position and shape, the named TermMode bits TD reads (rio.rs READ_MODES: bits 0-17; the kitty keyboard bits are masked off on both cores), the history size and the screen size. observed is true, false or "partly"; anything not fully observed says why. Each match is a regular expression over the token names unknowns.py produces, matched whole. unknowns.py reports every family as checked, partly, unseen or never sent, and every token no family names as uncatalogued.

families.name: wide characters (CJK, fullwidth)
families.how: row text, wide flags in the style runs

families.name: invalid UTF-8
families.how: row text (what each core prints instead)

families.name: BEL (bell)
families.why: the bell is an event sent to the window, not screen state

families.name: HT (tab)
families.how: cursor, and the tab kept in the cell

families.name: other C0 controls, NUL, DEL
families.how: row text: ignored bytes must leave nothing behind

families.name: ESC 7 / ESC 8 (save, restore cursor)
families.how: cursor, and the style of later text

families.name: ESC D / E / M (index, next line, reverse index)
ESC \ (string terminator alone)
families.how: row text: must leave nothing behind

families.name: CSI cursor movement (CUU CUD CUF CUB CNL CPL CHA CUP HVP VPA VPR HPR HPA)
CSI J / K / X (erase in display, line, characters)
CSI @ P L M (insert, delete characters and lines)
CSI g / I / Z (clear tabs, forward and back tab)
CSI s / u (save, restore cursor, SCO)
CSI SP q (cursor style)
families.why: the shape is recorded; whether it blinks is not

families.name: CSI " q (character protection)
families.why: protection is not a cell flag TD keeps

families.name: CSI t (window operations, title stack)
families.why: window reports and the title stack are not screen state

families.name: device attribute and status queries (CSI c, > c, = c, n, ? n, x)
families.why: the answers go back to the program, and the lab records the screen

families.name: CSI $ p (request a mode)
families.why: the answer goes back to the program

families.name: kitty keyboard protocol (CSI > u, < u, = u, ? u)
families.why: TD encodes keys itself and masks the kitty keyboard modes off on both cores

families.name: xterm key modifiers (CSI > m, > n)
families.why: key encoding is TD's, not the core's

families.name: SGR bold, dim, italic, underline, inverse, hidden, strike, double underline
SGR 5 / 6 / 25 (blink)
families.why: TD keeps no blink flag, so neither core's answer is recorded

families.name: SGR 53 / 55 (overline)
families.why: TD keeps no overline flag

families.name: SGR fonts, frames, super and subscript (10-20, 26, 50-52, 54, 60-65, 73-75)
families.why: no cell flag records them

families.name: DECSET 5 (reverse video)
families.why: screen-wide reverse video is not a mode TD reads

families.name: DECSET 8 (key autorepeat)
families.why: keyboard behaviour, not screen state

families.name: DECSET 12 (cursor blink)
families.why: blinking is not recorded

families.name: DECSET 69 (left and right margins)
families.why: not a mode TD reads; neither core claims it

families.name: DECSET 9 / 1001 (X10, highlight mouse)
families.why: rio-vt keeps X10 mouse above bit 17, which TD masks off

families.name: DECSET 1015 / 1016 (urxvt, pixel mouse)
families.why: not a mode TD reads

families.name: DECSET 1034 / 1036 / 1039 (meta key handling)
families.why: keyboard behaviour, not screen state

families.name: DECSET 2026 (synchronized update)
families.why: TD handles it in front of the core (vt/text.rs); the lab records state, not when a frame may be drawn

families.name: DECSET 2027 (grapheme clustering)
families.why: TD drops it in front of the core (vt/text.rs)

families.name: DECSET 2031 (colour scheme reports)
families.why: reports go back to the program

families.name: DECSET 2048 (in-band resize reports)
families.why: reports go back to the program

families.name: SM 2 / 12 (keyboard lock, local echo)
families.why: not modes TD reads

families.name: OSC 0 / 1 / 2 (window and icon title)
families.why: the title is an event sent to the window, not screen state

families.name: OSC 4 / 104 (palette colours)
families.why: cells record a colour's index, not the colour the palette gives it

families.name: OSC 7 (working directory)
families.why: an event, not screen state

families.name: OSC 8 (hyperlinks)
families.why: observe() records no hyperlink on a cell

families.name: OSC 9 / 777 / 99 (notifications)
families.why: an event, not screen state

families.name: OSC 10 / 11 / 12 and 110-112 (default colours, queries)
families.why: default colours and their answers are not cell state

families.name: OSC 22 (pointer shape)
families.why: not screen state

families.name: OSC 52 (clipboard)
families.why: TD does not act on it; an event, not screen state

families.name: OSC 133 (shell prompt marks)
families.why: prompt marks are not recorded

families.name: OSC 1337 (iTerm2 extensions)
families.why: not screen state the lab records

families.name: DCS $ q (request a setting)
families.why: the answer goes back to the program

families.name: DCS + q (terminfo query)
families.why: the answer goes back to the program

families.name: DCS q (sixel pictures)
families.why: pictures are not recorded

families.name: DCS = 1 s / = 2 s (old synchronized update)
families.why: frame timing, not state

families.name: APC G (kitty graphics)
families.why: pictures are not recorded

families.name: PM, SOS and other APC strings
families.how: row text: an ignored string must leave nothing behind

families.name: an escape sequence cut off by the end of the case
families.how: row text, and whatever the next case would see
